bulk.caution: Single committed sample; cluster WAL includes concurrent/checkpoint effects if any. EXPLAIN temp blocks do not expose all trigger-internal temporary IO.

judge.apiInstanceEvidence: Single createApp fixture and submit helper in immutable Back/test/judge-capacity.pipeline-spec.ts; no multi-API wave field or experiment exists.
limitations: Three eight-job waves are a finite regression campaign, not sustained saturation or a production capacity bound.
No campaign warmup submissions. Earlier tests may have warmed the shared executor; wave drift is descriptive, not causal.
Nearest-rank percentiles: per-wave p95/p99 are maxima; aggregate n=24 p99 is the maximum. No population-tail estimate.
Active throughput includes admission HTTP and completion observation, but excludes quota waits and consistency queries. Wall throughput includes startup, all waits, verification and worker shutdown.
Worker CPU and lifetime peak RSS cover the two owned Node PIDs only; API/DB/Redis and compiler/executor resources are not included.
All cases expect AC. This is not a full eight-language verdict/memory matrix or a before/after optimization comparison.

phase2ScalingTrials.scope: Disposable API/PostgreSQL/Redis, real workers and go-judge; eight accepted languages, one sample/job, alternating 1/2/2/1 worker trials after Python warmup.
limitations: Eight jobs/trial: p95/p99 are sample maxima, not steady-state tail estimates.
Jobs/s measures admitted bursts; per-IP 20/minute admission pauses are recorded outside the timed interval.
Shared CI runner; no production capacity or before/after optimization claim.
Worker CPU uses owned-PID procfs tick deltas; peak RSS includes warmup. API also hosts the test harness: isolated API CPU/RSS is not reported.
Proxy faults interrupt worker TCP links, not Redis/API services. Natural lease expiry uses real time.

actual clean owned Redis daemon restart with AOF and mixed queued work
accepted generation 1, interrupted rejudge generation 2, natural recovery generation 3

limitations: One CI browser/viewport, warm cache, no CPU/network throttling, two-submission fixture.
Small dependent samples do not establish population p95/p99, device-wide performance or before/after improvement.
Observers and DOM checks add measurement overhead; late paints/shifts outside each bounded window are not measured.
Unsupported metrics are null with reasons; functional API/UI assertions remain required without latency pass thresholds.

observedCandidates.acceptanceScope: PR89 component source has complete successful CI; this is not a later PR91/final integration execution or a substitute for independent QA acceptance.

protocol.scope: Real frontend editor with deterministic browser-routed mock API and synthetic authentication; no real backend, native executor or provider.
protocol.budgetScope: Actions, autosave and heap sampling; observer disposal/reporting use the remaining 90-second test ceiling.
protocol.actionWallTiming: Includes automation, assertions and the mock autosave debounce; not a processing/paint latency.
protocol.clocks: Actions use Node monotonic time; heap/EventTiming use browser monotonic time from probe installation. These nearby origins are not identical.

eventTiming.quantileScope: Retained thresholded event entries only, not independent interactions; a full buffer keeps the early prefix and discards later entries.

fieldINP.reason: A finite automated laboratory interaction sample is not field INP.

limitations: Heap values are optional nonstandard browser JS-heap estimates, may be coarse or shared, and exclude whole-platform/native memory.
The page, instrumentation and browser runtime contribute to the heap; this does not isolate editor allocation.
One 40-second schedule cannot establish a leak, absence of leaks, long-term capacity, a speedup or a population latency distribution.
EventTiming is thresholded and may be empty, rounded, unsupported or truncated. No latency or heap-size acceptance threshold is imposed.
Every reported heap estimate in this run is identical and coarse; zero recorded change does not establish zero allocation or absence of a leak.
The EventTiming buffer was full: 200 early entries retained and 176 later delivered filtered entries discarded. Quantiles cover the retained prefix only.
Edit-autosave and file-toggle wall intervals include automation and assertions and remain separate distributions; browser and Node time origins are not identical.

methodology.comparison: Current-source qualification only; no baseline/candidate optimization or speedup is claimed.
methodology.reads: One warmup then five serial complete query samples; EXPLAIN ANALYZE is separate from timed samples.
methodology.writes: One committed 256-row bulk rejudge and one deliberately rolled-back reverse transition, each with full recount oracle.
methodology.quantiles: n=5 nearest-rank p95/p99 equal the observed maximum, not population-tail estimates.
methodology.resources: Node client CPU/RSS and database size; PostgreSQL CPU/RSS/pool-saturation/IO-rate are not measured. EXPLAIN buffers/WAL and cluster-LSN WAL are scoped observations.
methodology.constraints: Fixed synthetic fixture; no HTTP/Redis/Judge/XP capacity or production migration/RTO/RPO claim.

declaredWorkflowServiceCaps.scope: Declarations verified in retained workflow source, not measured service peak memory or CPU.

limitations: Different host/runtime/settings from local execution; no causal before/after speedup or regression claim.
All read queries are serial and warmed. SQL driver transfer/decoding is timed; full HTTP/CSV serialization is outside this interval.
Node RSS values are endpoint samples of the client retaining data/evidence, not PostgreSQL/API peak RSS or isolated allocation.
Full EXPLAIN JSON is retained in the original report. Parent/child buffer values are not summed; EXPLAIN execution is separate from timed queries.
Cluster WAL endpoints are not retained for independent LSN subtraction. Reported cluster WAL and plan WAL have different scopes.
Trigger-internal temporary IO and actual transition-table source materialization are not fully measured.

bounded fixture with product history and transition pressure

limitations: One finite synthetic fixture, not production RTO/RPO or capacity.
No production connection or existing database is modified.
work_mem pressure does not establish measured spill volume or peak PostgreSQL RSS.
Empty rollback/reapply and populated final-migration refusal are distinct checks; full-chain checks remain in check-migrations.mjs.
Seeded product/XP history is synthetic; reference integrity is not API authorization or live award execution.
No before/after performance improvement is claimed.
One rehearsal and one timing per stage, not statistical recovery-success rates or production RTO/RPO.
The ZIP retains the report, not the dump archive or table data. Offline verification checks report integrity/counts, not a replay of dump/restore or row-hash computation.
Full schema/table comparison and populated rollback refusal were executed by the harness; retained fingerprints are that execution's observations.

multiApi.topology: Two actual dist/main.js child processes and two actual Judge/dist/worker.js child processes on one disposable CI host; one shared PostgreSQL database, Redis database and native executor.
limitations: One finite eight-job protocol, not a saturation, capacity, p95/p99, long-term memory or production fault-domain measurement.
A bounded observer resets test Redis throttle counters once before owned API setup; no counter resets, extra solver accounts, bypass headers or retries occur during the protocol.
The API clients use loopback URLs; actual listeners are separately observed by PID and socket inode. This does not establish a firewall or production network policy.
Queue timestamps and API/DB dates are host wall clocks; worker phase durations use performance.now. Queue start/finish bracket BullMQ work, not native instruction execution.
One procfs resource sample per owned child and cumulative worker metrics describe Node processes, not native compilers, sandbox processes or total host resource use.
Claim checks cover one observed active Go lease and terminal claims; no API, Redis or native outage is injected.
Derived nearest-rank n8 p95/p99 equal maxima of this finite sample, not population-tail estimates.
DB createdAt/updatedAt are observed row timestamp values, not commit timestamps or native execution boundaries. Their overlap3 is distinct from BullMQ overlap2.
Process CPU is cumulative since each child started; no before-snapshot exists. Do not sum cumulative per-job worker counters or call endpoint CPU the eight-job CPU cost.
Per-child RSS/peak excludes native compiler/executor, PostgreSQL, Redis and host resources. V8 old-space limits are not whole-process RSS caps.
Recorded elapsed time includes cleanup but is sampled before report serialization/write/upload. Active interval includes HTTP, polling and cross-API result reads.
Worker distribution6+2 and the long Go job are retained; this is not a fairness guarantee, steady-state capacity or saturation run.
